description:
PROBLEM
There is no way to fork a live queue to test a workflow variant and discard it. The motivating scenario (operator, 2026-07-03): "what if I changed the delivery workflow from x to y" — pause a production delivery queue, branch it at a position, run the variant against the branch, compare, discard. TD-009 (docs/helix/02-design/technical-designs/TD-009-experimentation-pause-branch-read-as-of.md) designs the mechanics.

CURRENT STATE
- Object-log manifest and segment objects are immutable and per-(tenant,queue): ManifestEntry (crates/pqueue-objectlog/src/segmented.rs:539-549), shard_prefix (:582) — already copy-on-write-shaped.
- Leases/epochs are per-queue with a single-active-lease invariant (crates/pqueue-engine/src/control_plane.rs:14,59-89).
- Segment retention/expiry exists per TD-004 and is unaware of cross-queue references.
- read_as_of and intake-blocking pause land in dependency beads.

PROPOSED FIX
Per TD-009 section 3-4: branch(source_shard, at: CommandPosition) -> new QueueKey. Object-log: allocate a new queue identity Q-prime (new prefix + manifest series) whose manifest references the parent's immutable segment objects for sequences <= P (no data copy), diverging with its own segments after; Q-prime acquires its own control-plane lease/epoch (parent fence untouched); emit_change_records=false by default on branches; branch carries a TTL and pins the parent's segments <= P against expiry until the branch is discarded. Relational family: structured capability-unavailable until the ADR-013 rebuild-from-log migration. Document the inherited-lease behavior (reconstructed Leased items expire on the normal clock in the branch) and the shared idempotency namespace <= P.

NON-SCOPE
- Comparison/diff tooling. Automatic branch GC beyond TTL. Relational branch implementation.
title: Branch-at-position: copy-on-write queue fork on the object-log manifest

description:
Snorri/Cayce needs pqueue to provide an authoritative StateStore boundary before Snorri can replace Cayce's internal workflow runtime in production.

Current evidence from sibling snorri, run against pqueue revision a7401c1:
- `cargo run -p snorri-spike-pqueue -- --source-audit --format markdown` passes its audit harness but reports blocking gaps: no public vectorized claimed-work commit, public upsert/ack/finalize do not accept caller request ids, public ack is item-id shaped instead of lease-token claim-ref shaped, backend data-plane envelopes still build `request_id: None`, `QueueIdempotencyCache` is documented as not wired through push/claim/finalize, RESP is worker/interoperability only, and non-work side records/recovery reads are missing.
- `cargo run -p snorri-spike-pqueue -- --prototype --format markdown` proves the public Rust facade can express Snorri input/state/audit/outbox/await records, but only as multiple public operations: upsert input, claim input, upsert state, push audit, upsert outbox, upsert await, ack input. That is not one recoverable transition boundary.

Required pqueue capability:
Expose a public Rust API for a vectorized claimed-work commit suitable for Snorri transition commits. Each vector entry must atomically validate a lease-token-bearing claim reference, apply bounded opaque non-work side-record writes for workflow state and audit, apply ordinary queue lifecycle writes for dispatchable outbox/await/timer work as needed, advance or validate a caller-supplied instance/state fence, finalize the input claim, and return a per-entry outcome. The API must accept caller-supplied request ids so Snorri can derive stable transition request ids from durable workflow inputs and rely on retained replay/conflict/expired outcomes.

Detailed requirements:
- Public Rust facade exposes a native claimed-work commit operation, not only hidden engine ports.
- Commit request includes caller request id or per-entry transition request id; same body replays, different body conflicts, expired idempotency metadata returns a structural expired outcome.
- Commit entries carry a claim reference with item id, lease token, lease expiry, and item version/fence. Public finalization must not depend only on item id.
- Commit validates claim authority and state/item fence inside the same durable boundary as side-record writes and input finalization.
- Backend command-envelope construction propagates request ids instead of building data-plane envelopes with `request_id: None` for this path.
- QueueIdempotencyCache or equivalent retained request-id machinery is wired into the accepted data-plane commit path.
- Side records intended for authoritative state/audit are not ordinary claimable work. Provide generic non-work opaque records, an equivalent documented non-work convention with conformance tests, or a capability-declared adapter-owned table boundary. Outbox effects, due timers, and awaits may remain ordinary queue lifecycle records when claim/finalize semantics are intended.
- Capability descriptors must let Snorri reject unsupported backends before activation: atomic transition commit, vectorized commit, lease validation, retained commit idempotency, non-work side records, authoritative recovery reads, delayed awaits/timers where advertised, and clear durability/consistency boundary.
- Recovery/explain reads expose enough committed records to decide retry/replay and explain instance state: transition request id, workflow instance key/fence, consumed input event id, side-record writes, outbox/await/timer records, and per-entry commit status.
- RESP is explicitly out of scope for authoritative Snorri StateStore MVP unless it grows an equivalent Rust-finalizable claim/ref and request-id commit boundary. RESP can remain worker/interoperability surface.

In-scope areas:
- crates/pqueue/src/lib.rs public facade and public types
- crates/pqueue-engine command envelopes, idempotency, finalize validation, backend write/command composition, and capability descriptors
- memory/sqlite/postgres/objectlog backend data-plane plumbing needed by the new boundary
- projection/recovery reads needed to prove the committed records are visible and replay-safe
- tests/contract fixtures proving the boundary across at least memory and one durable backend

Out of scope for this bead:
- Making pqueue understand Snorri workflow categories such as workflow state, audit, effect, or await. Payloads should stay opaque to pqueue.
- Choosing tenant/job semantics for Snorri or Cayce. Cayce/Snorri create unique queues per workflow/run; pqueue should not need Cayce tenant id or job id beyond opaque queue identity and caller metadata.
- RESP parity for authoritative state commits.
- Cayce-side migration code.
title: Expose Snorri authoritative vectorized claimed-work commit

description:
PROBLEM
Snorri's saga/workflow-state design (epic pqueue-2201fd37, "Snorri authoritative-commit boundary") is meant to let most single-transaction saga-step work happen INSIDE pqueue's own atomic commit boundary (CommitTransitionPort: validate a lease/version claim ref, write opaque side records, enqueue next-step lifecycle items, advance a caller instance/state fence, and finalize the consumed input claim -- all atomically, per entry). This is fully implemented and advertised on pqueue-memory (via the generic composed backend) and pqueue-sqlite's relational family (crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:5731, all capabilities true, DurabilityClass::Atomic).

Postgres -- the actual production/Lakebase deployment target for Snorri -- does NOT implement it. Do not route normal data-plane commands through a local transaction that is acknowledged before object-log durability. description:
PROBLEM
Snorri/Cayce needs hot workflow visibility before completed actions are archived to Niflheim/ClickHouse. Current pqueue projection reads (`peek`, `claimed`, `live_items`, `metrics`, exact typed index lookups) are not enough for Cayce-style operational reporting over scheduled workflow actions while the queue is hot.

7th Sense reference shape inspected from `/Users/erik/Projects/7thsense/master`:
- `interfaces/graphile/postgraphile/src/services/jobActionsChartService.ts` groups hot/cold action rows by `toStartOfHour(scheduledTimestamp)`, `status`, `suppressedByRecycling`, and `schedulerAlgorithm`; segments `engagementProbability`; and reports recycling details.
- `infrastructure/postgres/src/main/scala/ss/postgres/quill/QuillScheduledActionsPersistence.scala` creates scheduled actions, claims due actions by `jobId/type/status/scheduledTimestamp`, calculates hourly/status/algorithm/engagement buckets, counts pending/remaining actions, and applies status-update rules for engagement class and open-rate filter membership.
- `interfaces/graphile/db/postgres/dump.sql` defines `jobs_scheduled_actions` with indexes on `(job_id)`, `(job_id, scheduled_timestamp, status)`, `(parent_job_id, target_key)`, and `delivery_id`.

Snorri should expose the workflow query language to Cayce/MCP, but pqueue must provide the generic hot indexed projection substrate underneath it. pqueue must stay domain-neutral: do not add Snorri-specific workflow semantics, source-map concepts, Cayce open-rate vocabulary, or long-retention analytics. It should provide typed indexed record/query primitives with bounded aggregation and safe mutation semantics that Snorri can use to implement its own workflow visibility API.

REQUIRED HOT RECORD SHAPE
The contract must support queue items and non-claimable side/projection records carrying typed indexed fields equivalent to this domain-neutral example:

```json
{
  "record_type": "scheduled_action_projection",
  "tenant_id": "tenant_7s",
  "account_id": "acct_42",
  "workflow_id": "wf_nurture",
  "run_id": "job_9001",
  "instance_id": "inst_contact_001",
  "action_id": "act_001",
  "target_key": "contact:001",
  "action_type": "message.send",
  "status": "scheduled",
  "scheduled_at": "2026-07-02T14:00:00Z",
  "completed_at": null,
  "scheduler_algorithm": "personalized",
  "engagement_probability": 0.0825,
  "engagement_threshold": 0.10,
  "suppressed_by_recycling": true,
  "is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter": false,
  "payload": {"message_ref":"welcome_email","contact_open_rate_state":{"openRate":0.0825,"runningRate":0.096,"isOptOut":false}}
}
```

REQUIRED QUERY SHAPES
1. Detail page query: filter by tenant/account/run/action/status/scheduled range; order by scheduled_at, completed_at, status, scheduler_algorithm, engagement_probability, or stable id; return cursor-paginated rows.
2. Hourly distribution query: `tenant_id = T AND run_id = R AND action_type = message.send AND scheduled_at >= start AND scheduled_at < end GROUP BY hour(scheduled_at), status ORDER BY hour`.
3. Recycling preview query substrate: same scheduled range, grouped by hour and `suppressed_by_recycling`, with filter expressions over `engagement_probability`, `engagement_threshold`, and `is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter`.
4. Engagement segment query substrate: group by declared numeric buckets over `engagement_probability` (0, 0-1, 1-2, ..., 9-10, 10-15, ..., 95-100, no-activity).
5. Safe bounded mutation substrate: scan/update records for a run where `status = scheduled AND is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter = false`, setting status/suppression projection fields with per-record CAS or equivalent compare-and-set so concurrent claims/commits cannot lose updates.
6. Claim due work by query: claim records by `tenant_id/run_id/action_type/status/scheduled_at <= as_of` in scheduled_at order, returning lease tokens and item versions compatible with the existing claimed-work commit/finalize boundary.

EXPECTED INDEXES
At minimum, tests must define and exercise these typed compound indexes or equivalent query plans:
- `(tenant_id, run_id, scheduled_at)` range/order index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, status, scheduled_at)` pending/due/status index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, action_type, scheduled_at)` action distribution index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, suppressed_by_recycling, scheduled_at)` recycling bucket index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, scheduler_algorithm, scheduled_at)` algorithm bucket index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, engagement_probability)` numeric segment source index.
- `(tenant_id, run_id, target_key)` unique lookup/upsert index.

EXAMPLE FIXTURE DATA
Seed at least these records in a shared conformance fixture:

```json
[
  {"action_id":"act_001","target_key":"contact:001","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T14:05:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.0825,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":true,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":false},
  {"action_id":"act_002","target_key":"contact:002","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T14:37:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.1280,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true},
  {"action_id":"act_003","target_key":"contact:003","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T15:02:00Z","status":"suppressed","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"randomized","engagement_probability":0.0000,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":true,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":false},
  {"action_id":"act_004","target_key":"contact:004","scheduled_at":"2026-07-02T15:45:00Z","status":"scheduled","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"randomized","engagement_probability":null,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true},
  {"action_id":"act_005","target_key":"contact:005","scheduled_at":"2026-07-03T09:15:00Z","status":"failed","action_type":"message.send","scheduler_algorithm":"personalized","engagement_probability":0.4510,"engagement_threshold":0.10,"suppressed_by_recycling":false,"is_enrolled_using_open_rate_filter":true},

]
```

- Niflheim/ClickHouse archival analytics.

description: Under CPU starvation / high host load, multi-node object_log_sqlite_projection collapses ~36x (8-owner worst per-queue 3300/s -> 87/s) instead of degrading gracefully. ROOT CAUSE (code-traced): each node runs its own InMemoryControlPlane (sole owner of its disjoint queues). When the background renew_sessions task runs late under load, the lease TTL (15s) lapses; cp_resolve reports Unassigned; the node re-acquires via lease_decide_acquire (control_plane.rs:126) which UNCONDITIONALLY does assignment_epoch+1. That epoch bump fences the node's OWN in-flight pushes/claims (EpochFenced / -ERR pqueue epoch_stale) -> client retry storm -> under continued starvation repeats -> collapse. A slow-but-alive owner fences itself. FIX: re-affirming ownership of one's OWN uncontested lease (current.active_owner == acquiring owner) must PRESERVE assignment_epoch (refresh lease_expires_at only); epoch advances ONLY on takeover by a DIFFERENT owner. Safe: if the authority record still names us active_owner, no other owner acquired in the gap. Result: graceful degradation. Exposed by pqueue-36d405a9's live cargo test failing its 8-owner sweep under host load ~13 on a 12-core box.
